title: Fleet stock rotation and import windows
content:
Purpose:
This is a working note describing a complementary approach to our existing procurement pipeline: an explicit stock-rotation and import-window plan that reduces cold-start capacity deficits, evens SKU mix across regions, and minimizes cross-region transfer costs. This doc focuses on calendarized purchase spacing, vendor lane prioritization, and rack-level staging ("pre-warm pools") rather than only aggregate order volumes.

Background / why this matters now:
- Q4 usage volatility + new large customers in APAC exposed gaps between lead-time assumptions and when units are actually usable.
- Our bulk-order cadence has been optimized for price, but we see localized shortages (west-eu and apac) while na samples sit idle in northamerica depots waiting for rack space.
- Transfers between regions cost ~20% of unit price (transport + customs + re-qualification). Better import-window planning reduces those transfers.

High-level goals (measurable):
1) Keep regional availability >= 95% of target capacity for 99% of days (target capacity = committed SLA headroom + 10% buffer).
2) Reduce cross-region transfers by 50% over the next 12 months.
3) Establish a rolling 6-month calendar with PO milestones and "pre-warm" staging targets per AZ/rack.

Assumptions used in this draft (call these out and validate):
- Current fleet (live): NA: 4,200 A100-equivalent, EU: 1,800, APAC: 600 (numbers normalized to A100-Eq).
- Monthly gross burn: 120 A100-Eq units (expansion + churn).
- Preferred vendors: Vendor-A (stable supply, 9–12 week lead), Vendor-B (shorter lead 6–8 wks but higher price), Distributor-C (spot availability, 3–6 wks on special lanes).
- Customs + staging average delay: NA inbound = 1 wk, EU inbound = 1.5 wk, APAC inbound = 2–3 wk (varies by port).

Stock-rotation concept (summary):
Instead of treating inventory as static regional buckets, we schedule overlapping "rotation windows" per SKU that:
- Spread receipts over time (avoid big monolithic receipts that create ephemeral overcapacity and then deficits),
- Prioritize arrival to regions with negative forecast delta, and
- Intentionally overbuy in low-cost lanes to establish a short-term pre-warm pool for spike absorption.

Concrete structure (rolling 6-month calendar):
- Calendar is divided into 6 discrete import windows (1 per 30 days). For each window we define: expected PO slice, vendor lane, destination region(s), and staging target (rack-ready units).
- Target pre-warm pool size per region = max(10% of regional target capacity, 30 units). This acts as immediate absorb buffer for canary bursts.
- Example: Window 1 (Dec): Vendor-B -> NA (1,000 units split as 600 racked NA, 200 pre-warm pool NA depot, 200 held for EU transfer if needed).

Vendor lane prioritization (heuristic):
- Lane 1 (preferred): Vendor-A bulk shipments to NA → prioritize NA racking, small tranche forwarded to EU by sea.
- Lane 2 (fast): Vendor-B express shipments to EU/APAC where lead time sensitivity is high.
- Lane 3 (opportunistic): Distributor-C spot buys routed to closest depot and used to backfill pre-warm pools.

Lead-time table (working assumptions, validate with procurement):
- Vendor-A (NA factory lane): 9–12 weeks manufacturing + 1 week inbound NA + 2–3 days local racking
- Vendor-A (EU lane via sea): 10–14 weeks + 1.5 week port delay + 1 week customs and rack prep
- Vendor-B (air/express): 6–8 weeks + 0.5–1 week inbound
- Distributor-C (regional stock): 3–6 weeks (high variance)

Regional staging & rack assignment rules:
- Rack readiness target: units assigned to rack within 10 business days of arrival to the local depot.
- For multi-AZ regions, spread new units across AZs to avoid correlated failure exposures (no >40% of a SKU family in single AZ).
- Reserve 1 rack / 48 units per region as a "warm standby" for urgent re-routes.

Utilization smoothing via pre-warm pools:
- Pre-warm pools live in depots (not yet racked in production) and have a 'spin-up' time of ~48–72 hours to move to rack and qualify.
- Pools used for: immediate capacity surges, canary testing of new SKU builds, and hardware failure replacement within SLO.

Risk matrix (key items):
- Long vendor lead times + single-supplier dependency for new newer-gen SKUs. Mitigation: staggered BRD with backup distributor lanes.
- Port congestion (APAC) causing 2–4 week variance. Mitigation: increase pre-warm target for APAC by +50% for next 3 windows.
- Regulatory hold-ups (temporary import paperwork). Mitigation: pre-submit customs docs and maintain a local broker SLA.

Cost tradeoffs (notes):
- Spreading purchases increases per-unit short-term price (fewer volume discounts) but reduces transfer/carry costs and risk. We should run a 12-month TCO model (finance help).
- Pre-warm pools carry storage + insurance costs (~$X/unit/month placeholder) — needs modeling.

Short PO cadence proposal (example values — to be validated):
- Month 0 window: 600 units (Vendor-B express to EU/APAC), 400 units (Vendor-A to NA)
- Month 1 window: 500 units (Vendor-A to NA with 200 earmarked for NA pre-warm), 200 units (Distributor-C opportunistic)
- Month 2 window: 800 units (Vendor-A bulk), shift 150 units sea-forwarded to EU
- (This is illustrative; actual numbers to be reconciled with procurement and finance.)

Operational action items (owners):
- Priya D: run a sensitivity TCO model for 6 vs 12-month spread (jira INFRA-3421) — due 2024-11-22.
- Marco A: confirm Vendor-A lane lead times + minimum tranche sizes; negotiate split shipments (vendor-a-ship-terms doc) — due 2024-11-18.
- Jia C: prototype pre-warm pool playbook (steps: intake, quarantine, rack-test, fast-route) and a checklist for 48–72h spin-up — due 2024-11-30.
- Aisha P: confirm customs broker SLAs in APAC ports and produce contingency routing matrix — due 2024-11-25.

Open questions / to validate:
- Exact unit cost of storing pre-warm pools per depot (ops/finance).
- What is the practical max % we can defer racking before warranty/qualification constraints kick in?
- Are there contractual minimums that force us into >1 bulk tranche per vendor? (procurement clarification).

Notes to self / rough brainstorm bits:
- Consider short-term dedicated "air-lane" buys for enterprise launches (pay premium for 2–3 week ramp).
- Explore a swap pool arrangement with a colocation partner in EU to avoid sea shipments for urgent replenishment.
- Build a simple dashboard: rolling 6-window view, colored by risk (lead-time variance, percent pre-warm achieved, cross-region transfer exposure).

References/links:
- confluence: fleet-cost-modeling (placeholder)
- jira:INFRA-3421 (procurement sensitivity)
- github:repo/inventory-utils#87 (scripts for regional allocations)

This is a draft. Primary intent is to get alignment on the concept (stock-rotation + pre-warm pools) and surface concrete calendarized PO options that procurement can run against vendor lanes. Feedback welcome — especially from procurement and logistics on realistic lead times and tranche constraints.

-- Priya
summary: Working draft describing a rolling 6-month stock-rotation plan with pre-warm depot pools, calendarized PO windows, vendor lane prioritization, and action items to reduce cross-region transfers and smooth utilization.
